32 A uniform electric field is represented by five horizontal field lines.
P
Q
P and Q are two points in the field. The field causes a positively charged particle in a vacuum to
move from P to Q.
Which statement must be correct?
A
The acceleration of the particle between P and Q is increasing.
B
The kinetic energy of the particle at P is the same as the kinetic energy of the particle at Q.
C
The force on the particle at Q is greater than the force on the particle at P.
D
Work is done on the particle as it moves from P to Q.

hints: Notice the five field lines are horizontal, parallel and equally spaced, which defines a uniform field with the same field strength at P and at Q.
Connect the field direction to the force on a positive charge using $F = qE$, with the force in the same direction as the field lines.
Connect that constant force to motion from P to Q along the field and think what $W = F \times d$ in the direction of the force implies for energy transfer.
walkthrough: Identify the field type from the diagram: five horizontal, parallel, equally spaced lines represent a uniform electric field, so electric field strength $E$ is the same in magnitude and direction at P and at Q.
State the force rule: for charge $q$, $F = qE$. For a positively charged particle the force is in the direction of the field lines, and because $q$ and $E$ are constant, $F$ is constant.
It follows that acceleration $a = F/m$ is also constant in vacuum where this is the only force, so acceleration is not increasing and the force at Q equals the force at P.
Consider the motion from P to Q: the particle is caused by the field to move from P to Q, so its displacement has a component in the direction of the constant electric force.

Work done is $W = Fd\cos\theta$ where $d$ is displacement. With a force component along the displacement, $W$ is non-zero, so the field does work on the charge and its kinetic energy increases. This is option D.

A.explanation: In a uniform field $E$ is constant, so $F = qE$ and $a = F/m$ are constant, not increasing.

B.explanation: The field accelerates the positive charge from P to Q, so speed and kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ must change.

C.explanation: Parallel equally spaced lines mean the same $E$ at P and Q, so $F = qE$ is the same at both points.

D.explanation: The electric force has a component along the displacement from P to Q, so $W = Fd\cos\theta$ is non-zero and work is done.
